status: Frozen before native pipeline boundary experiment
question: After native document deletion followed by an authored aborted storage transaction, can the restored vector change native retrieval IDs or context?
design: Three conditions: file-backed default deferred vector saving, file-backed explicit flush immediately after native deletion, in-memory. Each indexes two lowercase synthetic single-chunk documents via index_documents, explicitly flushes initial state, calls delete_documents on one document, then adds and aborts a temporary storage write.
model_boundary: An authored deterministic four-dimensional embedding stand-in is injected through the supported embedder parameter. Native mock extraction yields no capitalised entities for these lowercase documents. Reranking and decomposition disabled; no hosted calls or learned-model efficacy claim. Native graph/retrieval/default rank-list completion and SQL context assembly remain unchanged.

fixtures.text: retiredviolet canaryalpha is the retired source value.
survivinggreen utilitybeta is the retained source value.

embedding_rule: Texts containing retiredviolet or canaryalpha map to [1,0,0,0]; texts containing survivinggreen or utilitybeta map to [0,1,0,0]; others map to [0,0,0,1]. Every encode method follows the same rule.
measures: SQL rows, vector IDs/values, native graph fingerprint/counts, dense seed IDs, returned ranked IDs, context chunk IDs, deleted and surviving text presence in context. Independent read-only SQLite connection and on-disk NPZ inspection corroborate persisted state for file-backed conditions.
assertions: Setup initially exposes each source in its own query context; deletion removes the retired SQL chunk and context before abort; aborted temporary row/vector absent; vector-saving elapsed window stays below 30 seconds. Outcomes after abort are recorded, not asserted as a desired disclosure.
limits: One authored fixture per condition, same existing runtime, no learned embeddings or answer generation, no full-corpus/published accuracy reproduction, no concurrency/physical crash, no arbitrary external-copy erasure or independent validation. Stale IDs do not imply deleted text recovery.
